name: Q B R Sales Planner
prompt:
"Create a 'QBR Sales Planner' app with live data annotation capabilities. The data source is an annual sales target spreadsheet broken down by Account Manager and Quarter.

The app needs to:

Render a clustered bar chart of target vs. actual sales per account manager.

Allow users to click directly on any individual bar or table row to open an interactive 'Annotation Tooltip'. Inside this tooltip, the user can type custom context notes (e.g., 'Supply chain disruption delayed closing until Q3') and select an importance flag (High/Medium/Low).

Save these annotations into a local side-panel feed called the 'Context Log'. Changing global filters (like toggling between regions) must update the main view but keep the written annotations safely preserved and attached to their original data rows."

thought_process.interpretation: I interpreted this as a high-stakes executive dashboard for Quarterly Business Reviews. The focus is on the interplay between quantitative performance (Sales Targets vs. Actuals) and qualitative context (Annotations). I've built a robust state-management system to ensure that 'Context Logs' persist across filtering sessions, treating the Account Manager and Quarter as unique keys for data binding.
skills_utilized: Tailwind CSS for enterprise-grade UI styling
assumed_from_scratch: A hierarchical sales organizational structure with Account Managers assigned to specific regions.
A business logic layer to generate 'Actual' sales vs 'Target' sales ratios to make the visualization realistic.
A custom 'Floating Tooltip' positioning logic that responds to chart bar interactions.
thought_process.skill_suggestions: Future iterations should include a 'Bulk Annotation' mode for multiple quarters and a 'Snapshot' feature to export the QBR view as a PDF with the Context Log embedded.
